newsitem.title: INDIA: Enron India plant seen starting in Dec '98.
newsitem.headline: Enron India plant seen starting in Dec '98.

text.p: U.S. Enron Corporation's Indian unit said on Tuesday work on its maiden project was ahead of schedule, with more than 36 percent of construction complete on its 740 MW power plant on the western coast.
"The construction is 36 percent over and 84 percent of the engineering and procurement work is over," said an official of Dabhol Power Company (DPC), Enron's local subsidiary.
About 5,000 people are working at the site on the Maharashtra coast, including 400 employed by Bechtel Corporation, a U.S. firm owning 10 percent of DPC, he said.
"Almost all GE equipment has arrived at the site," he said, referring to General Electric Co, another U.S. firm owning 10 percent of the Indian firm. Enron owns 80 percent of DPC.

DPC is hoping to commission the plant by December 1998, ahead of the commencement date of April 1999 committed to in the power purchase agreement with the state utility Maharashtra State Electricity Board, the official said.
Up to March 31 DPC had spent $697 million of a total project cost of $1.08 billion for the first phase of 740 MW, he said.
In the southern state of Tamil Nadu, Enron has been awarded a contract to build a 240 MW naphtha fired power plant at Ranipet near the port city of Chennai, officials said.
